set.approach: Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that suits a high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicle, followed by a long approach to the base of the main climbing areas. Razorback is a small cragging formation tucked between the Southeast Buttress and the East Tower; the lines sit on its right-hand face as you hike up from below. Razorbutt is a short wide crack reached by hiking up the hillside and around to the back of the formation.

review.notes: Route and area pages. No descent text.

set.descent_text: A rappel anchor on the far side of the tower drops you into the gully. Single-rope rappels with a long rope work, with some fourth class downscrambling between; a large boulder with slings marks the next rappel station, which finishes in the bottom of the Keyhole.
set.approach: Prindle is reached by a rough road from Fairbanks that suits a high-clearance four-wheel-drive vehicle, followed by a long approach to the base of the main climbing areas. Head to the Main Wall; the Southeast Buttress is the feature on its right. Homewrecker starts in the low-angle grassy gully at the middle of the toe of the buttress, where most parties scramble the first pitch to a bolted station off to the left of the ramp.

review.notes: Route page gives the descent and start; area pages the road and buttress location.

set.approach: Cali Slit is in the Spirit Boulder Area at the Mile High Wall in the Reed Lakes basin of Hatcher Pass. Drive from Palmer up North Palmer Fishhook Road to the Mother Lode Lodge switchback, then onto Archangel Road, and walk the trail to the abandoned cabin where the climbing begins. The area lies left of the approach gully to the Shield, Main Wall and Two Toke Tower, and the route starts left of the Spirit Boulder Chalice.

review.notes: Route and area pages. No descent text.

set.approach: Park where the guardrail ends just past the 17 mile sign on the road out of Haines. Drop into the ditch and follow the creek past the culvert to a flagged trail into the woods, which leads to a boulder field. Go straight up to the wall, or take the trail up the right side of the boulder field to avoid loose rock and moss; it reaches the base of Chest Fur. Unnamed 4 is the obvious overhanging crack as you work right along the wall.
